scope: cross-run reconciliation; no final new-unique-bug count

entries.title: Queued cancellation can be overwritten by concurrent lifecycle writes
entries.evidence_limit: Controlled component timing; Lite adds public POC evidence. Reuses the earlier queued-abort finding.

entries.title: Deleting a listed job can terminate the only scheduling thread
entries.evidence_limit: Lite adds public admin API and restart-recovery evidence. Related to the earlier status-store failure family; independent root-cause count remains unsettled.

entries.title: A late RUNNING write can replace an already-published terminal outcome
entries.evidence_limit: Deliberate timing assistance; upstream confirms validity but has not shown natural occurrence.

entries.title: An early authoritative client failure can make START collection raise KeyError
entries.evidence_limit: Failure classification and diagnostics change; no extra resource leak or service loss demonstrated.

entries.title: A metadata refresh can restore SUBMITTED after a successful abort
entries.evidence_limit: A different metadata writer in the queued-abort family; independent counting remains unsettled.

entries.title: Competing cleanup paths can terminate the completion thread with KeyError
entries.evidence_limit: Controlled competing cleanup schedule; no full deployment trigger retained.

entries.title: Concurrent process removal can terminate dead-client cleanup
entries.evidence_limit: Covered by CR-6; retain this specific dead-client cleanup branch.

entries.title: Client resources can be freed while same-group descendants remain alive
entries.evidence_limit: Real child-process evidence; descendant lifecycle and physical GPU contention are not established.

entries.title: Running-job abort can succeed while the final status is COMPLETED
entries.source_novelty: KNOWN (cite: Specula historical MC-E; fix-status: unfixed)
entries.evidence_limit: Controlled abort/completion window. Same final mechanism as CR-32, despite conflicting original novelty labels.

entries.title: An authoritative client failure recorded after the completion outcome read can be published as success
entries.evidence_limit: Seeded component state and controlled failure/finalization ordering; production message timing unproven.

entries.title: A client failure accepted in the startup tracking gap can be lost before success is published
entries.evidence_limit: Startup tracking-gap component evidence; a complete fast-start/client-failure process schedule is still needed.

entries.title: Stale delete authorization can strand a running job and its admission slot
entries.evidence_limit: Controlled authorize/start/delete ordering; no complete admin interaction replay retained.

entries.title: Accepted noncanonical min_clients can repeatedly starve a later eligible job
entries.evidence_limit: Included in CR-4; validator, store and scheduler are real components, not a network submission test.

entries.title: Malformed job metadata variants can block later jobs beyond the modeled numeric-string case
entries.evidence_limit: Includes MC-13 and additional malformed metadata variants. Component validation; portable runner provided.

entries.title: Live dictionary iteration disrupts lifecycle services
entries.evidence_limit: Includes MC-7 and related iteration sites; do not count the aggregate and its branch twice.

entries.title: Fractional GPU accounting fails to restore eligible capacity
entries.evidence_limit: Fractional accounting loses exact boundary capacity; not permanent loss of the whole GPU. Portable component runner provided.

entries.title: Parent death leaves a child in notification retry
entries.evidence_limit: Real local processes and CellNet, with a minimal parent/child environment; full worker bootstrap not exercised.

entries.title: Disable leaves pending outcomes and slots until the grace expires
entries.evidence_limit: Pending outcome retention has a grace/timeout bound; contract and impact require review.

entries.title: Overlapping resource consumption changes another job's launch environment
entries.source_novelty: NEW (permitted git-history/in-tree search found related GPU/launcher commits, but no exact prior report/fix for this overlap mechanism; external issue/PR discussion search was prohibited by the continuation instructions)
entries.evidence_limit: Matches the earlier shared environment finding; physical GPU probing was stubbed.

entries.title: Later empty-resource jobs inherit a stale device binding
entries.evidence_limit: Sequential empty-resource variant of shared environment state; isolation contract and counting remain unsettled.

entries.title: Best-effort SJ status arrival loses an execution error
entries.evidence_limit: Seeded component state; needs a real zero-exit process plus sufficiently late status message.

entries.title: Ordinary local restart leaves persisted lifecycle state inconsistent
entries.evidence_limit: Seeded persisted state; complete shutdown/restart reproduction is not retained.

entries.title: Cleanup pop races the waiter's return-code observation
entries.evidence_limit: Controlled cleanup/return-code observation; depends on startup marker state and interacts with CR-17.

entries.title: Unsafe client failure during startup does not mark the job aborted
entries.evidence_limit: Unsafe-component startup stop differs from ordinary live abort; actual typed failure and registration timing need review.

entries.title: Empty participants alias the live registered-client dictionary
entries.evidence_limit: Wrong participant membership/notification shown; no final job hang or failure demonstrated.

entries.title: Abort before client registration is dropped before a late start
entries.evidence_limit: A normal launch hook can widen the window; later heartbeat handling may mitigate the late child.

entries.title: Client shutdown and restart lose ownership before child cleanup
entries.evidence_limit: Includes state injection; complete client restart and resource-ownership closure still needed.

entries.title: Re-registration replaces tokens still used by running-job participants
entries.evidence_limit: Notification omission shown; concrete job hang not demonstrated.

entries.title: Typed process failures change meaning across normalization and status mapping
entries.evidence_limit: Real child with custom launch/notification harness; failure classification changes without greater demonstrated harm.

entries.title: Fast SJ engine completion is overwritten by STARTED
entries.evidence_limit: Same final mechanism as CR-31. Deterministic Thread.start shim; portable component runner does not establish natural timing.

entries.title: Delayed SJ heartbeat marks normal completion aborted
entries.evidence_limit: Controlled heartbeat/completion order; terminal outcome classification, not training-data corruption.

entries.title: Post-spawn setup or cleanup exceptions break resource ownership
entries.evidence_limit: Hold: custom free_resources unconditionally raises; default-path exception producer unproven. Does not re-confirm the earlier post-spawn handoff finding.

entries.title: A pending restart or shutdown marker is removed by worker bootstrap
entries.evidence_limit: Marker/PID state injection; complete worker/lifecycle-wrapper race remains unproven.

entries.title: Partial deployment leaves workspace state relevant to later operations
entries.evidence_limit: Partial-deployment workspace retention is distinct from Lite TTL reservations; download contract needs review.

entries.title: CAN_NOT_SCHEDULE overwrites an acknowledged abort
entries.evidence_limit: Same broad queued-abort family, but job stays stopped and only the terminal reason changes.

entries.title: An ordinary cleanup exception escapes completion's narrow catch
entries.evidence_limit: Excluded by the source report: no admissible default-path exception producer was found.

entries.title: Global machine status differs from concurrent job state
entries.evidence_limit: Merge with CR-24; its original global-status concern resolved to the same STARTED/STOPPED mechanism.

entries.title: Lock/RPC ordering or late notifications affect cleanup progress
entries.source_novelty: KNOWN (cite: local-git:f2b0039e/#4613 and local-git:6d193a24/#4633; fix-status: fixed)
entries.evidence_limit: Merge with MC-9; conflicting original known-fixed/unfixed labels are not independent findings.

entries.title: Retained SJ status reference can replace a newer failure record
entries.evidence_limit: Outcome remains failure; only its classification changes. Severity needs separate review.
